newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on soft dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on soft dlr.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Friday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries as weakness in the Canadian dollar weighed on bond prices in very thin markets, dealers said.

"We've got a technically weak Canadian dollar," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett. "You'll find very few people that are coming into the market to buy on the dips."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$110.25 to yield 7.133 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 24/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 57 basis points from 50 basis points at Thursday's close.

Canadian bonds weakened as the currency drifted lower during the day to trade at C$1.3629 (US$0.7337) from this morning's open of C$1.3608 (US$0.7348). The dollar is now in a technically weak position and there is some concern it could broach key resistance levels to trade even softer, ABN's Pyle said.
As a result, there is little interest at this time to buy into a Canadian market which is already seeing thin volumes, analysts said.

"It's underperformance because no one cares. Volumes have been extremely light today," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital. "No one has any interest here in Canada to do anything."
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.07 to C$103.58 to yield 6.505 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.32 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 19 basis points from 12 basis points at Thursday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.94 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.92 percent.
